recipes.name: Seasoned Turkey Burgers
ingredients_raw: 1 (1 ounce) package dry onion soup mix

steps.text: Mix turkey, egg, onion soup mix, soy sauce, pepper, and garlic powder in a large bowl until well combined; refrigerate mixture for about 10 minutes, then form into 6 equal-sized patties.
Preheat an outdoor grill for medium-high heat and lightly oil the grate.

Cook turkey burgers on the preheated grill, turning once, until no longer pink in the center and the juices run clear, about 20 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read at least 165 degrees F (74 degrees C). Serve on buns.

raw_recipe.headline: Seasoned Turkey Burgers
raw_recipe.description: Homemade turkey burger seasoning made with garlic, pepper, and soy sauce makes the best turkey burgers. Easy to make and great for grilling seasoning.

review.reviewBody: Really great recipe and used many times. My recommendation is (combining many other recommendations): make sure you get the amount of turkey right. Many times people complain it’s too salty, but if you’re sure to get the right amount of turkey (which is 1 ½ lbs.) , it should be about right. Use about 1 and 3/4 lbs. of turkey (or hamburger!) instead of the recommended 1and ½ lbs., if you tend to be weary of salt. Cooking at a nice medium low heat does help if you are using leaner meat, otherwise the outside can get overdone. Definitely consider freezing the remaining patties in the freezer! They are GREAT to remove in the morning and throw on the grill for a quick meal later on.

I have made this recipe for years and it’s our favorite. It doesn’t state if the turkey is 80/20 or 93/7 or whatever. I use 93/7 and double the recipe each time. I also add a tablespoon of Montreal steak seasoning. Mix everything but the turkey first, then add the meat to have better distribution. I have found that adding a tablespoon or so of olive oil and having panko on hand is helpful because sometimes the mixture is really wet and sticky even without the oil. Note that they are stickier than regular beef burgers but should hold their shape when patted into burgers. I pat them into 4 oz burgers and freeze for later. Just as others have said, they give a beef burger a run for its money.

YUM! I had a 2.5 pound pack of ground turkey from Sam's club, and found this recipe. I added 1 tsp of garlic powder, used lower sodium soy sauce, and added 1 Tbsp of worcestershire sauce. I kept the amounts of everything else the same. I used a old peanut butter lid lined with plastic wrap to press the burgers, and I came out with 10. I grilled them, along with some other burgers for my husband. He really liked these burgers, and said whatever I did 'different' he really liked!

These were delicious!! I did however make a few changes. I used Worchestershire sauce instead of soy sauce, minced cloves of garlic instead of garlic powder, and added 2 Tbl of plain breadcrumbs. I cooked them on the Foreman for about 10-15 minutes and topped each burger with a slice of Reduced Fat Pepper Jack cheese! My boyfriend (who refuses to eat turkey burgers) loved them as well!!

I just made this recipe and it is fantastic! I used a package of beefy onion soup mix and I did add 3 tablespoons of plain Panko bread crumbs. it turns out I'm not sure if I even really needed them because killing them in the fridge for 10 minutes made an incredible difference. They held together beautifully on my grill pan and are wonderful. This will be a new staple in my house, thanks for the recipe.

Awesome turkey burgers! Great flavor and not at all dry, like turkey burgers can sometimes be. I omitted the pepper, only because I'm not a big fan of it. I used 1 lb. of ground turkey instead of 1 1/2 lb. so I cut the onion soup mix quantity in half. Also, onion soup mix tends to be salty so didn't want to over-do it. I added a slice of colby-jack cheese the last minute or so and covered the pan to melt. Love this recipe and will be making frequently!

Turkey burgers aren’t my favorite, but these are pretty good! The soup mix adds a deeper flavor, and these stay nice and moist….well, as long as you don’t overcook them! 20 minutes, as stated in the recipe, is much too long. I did 3.5 minutes per side and they were cooked through but still juicy. I served these with red onion, tomato, cheese and shredded lettuce. A nice alternative to beef.

I have made this recipe numerous times. The only change I made was to use grated fresh garlic, 2 cloves instead of garlic powder. This is a spectacular recipe, burgers turn out very flavorful and very juicy. I saute them for about 5 minutes a side. add a salad or hot vegigie and you have a terrific dinner or lunch. I eat them without the roll, just plain on the plate with a little Heinz spicy ketchup. YUM, YUM,YUM

I love these burgers! They are easy to put together, juicy and flavorful. I used 1 pound of foster farms ground turkey. To that I added 1 package of Lipton Onion Soup Mix and 1 garlic clove, egg, slightly beaten, little soy sauce and fresh ground black pepper. My patties may have been a little larger so I ended up with 5 instead of 6 burgers. They did not take long to cook up on the grill, about 20 minutes, only flipping once. I served these on hamburger buns with thick slices of local tomatoes and manoa lettuce. The burgers are well seasoned, nothing overpowering at all. They are juicy and tasty, not dry and not needing any extra condiments (ketchup, mustard, mayonnaise, etc) to the burgers. The preparation, ingredients and cooking time are approximate. I served the burgers along with, "Baked Sweet Potato Sticks," also from this website. These baked sweet potatoes are also VERY good by the way and complement the turkey burgers nicely.

my family loved this! i substituted liquid smoke for the soy sauce because i have one child who doesn't like soy sauce. the burgers are really sticky, so don't forget to oil the grill, but they hold together nicely once they are cooked.

Good burger. You can switch the Lipton Onion dry dip mix for Laura Scutters green onion or toasted onion, if you wish. Also, you can always cook this on the stove at a lower heat, covered, which will help maintain the moisture. Do not smash the burger or poke holes in it. A little Avocado on your topping helps. Also, try honey mustard and sliced cheddar cheese melted on your burger. The small changes are the difference between night and day when it comes to a turkey burger.
I love this recipe. I also added green pepper and onions to the mix.
Very good! I will definitely make them again!
This was surprisingly good! Going to be a regular!

I was skeptical about serving turkey burgers to my guys but these were a surprise hit. Everyone really liked these and it was great to find something new. They were flavourful and had a good burger texture. Thanks for sharing this one! I wrote this review in 2009 and now I’m updating it in 2024. I used this recipe as inspiration for ground chicken and it was pretty good. We added fresh ginger and garlic, green onion, onion powder, Worcestershire and panko. Not bad at all. Served on toasted bun with lettuce, tomato and mayo. Don’t overcook or they will be dry, zero shrinking so don’t make them too big or thick, add oil to pan for crispy sides.
Delicious! Grateful there are no breadcrumbs in this recipe. The mixture is a bit sticky but refrigeration helps.
